subject.title: fix(sessions): drop dead-end orphan entries when retry forks parentId chain (#48810)

question: Should OpenClaw automatically delete a structurally valid but dead-end compaction entry during ordinary session-file load once cache coherence is repaired?
rationale: The PR changes persisted session history at load time; the compaction-only predicate reduces scope, but the acceptable recovery/deletion policy is a maintainer product and data-integrity choice.

options.title: Approve a narrow repair policy
options.body: Keep the compaction-only deletion rule, but require cache coherence and focused upgrade-safe tests before merge.

options.title: Move repair to explicit recovery
options.body: Keep detection and diagnostics but require a doctor or explicit repair action instead of mutating session history during normal load.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Leave the canonical issue open while maintainers determine whether compaction retry should instead be fixed at the writer path.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow repair policy
recommendation.body: Keep the compaction-only deletion rule, but require cache coherence and focused upgrade-safe tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the canonical session-fork evidence and are best positioned to validate whether the repair preserves the affected downstream reconstruction workflow.
